issues.title: Shared data model + seed.json with curated clip keys
issues.desc: Agree the Movie, tasteVector, and Session schemas (see PLAN.md §H and types.ts). Write `scripts/curate.mjs`: for ~60 movies, pull TMDB `/movie/{id}?append_to_response=videos,watch/providers`, prefer official `type == "Clip"` videos, then Teaser, then Trailer; fall back to a YouTube Data API v3 search restricted to the Movieclips channel; validate each key with `videos.list` (embeddable, not region-blocked for US, not age-restricted); write `key`, `start`, `end`, `source` into `seed.json`. Commit the output. Person C reviews the schema.
ac: seed.json has ~60 movies with poster, genres, keywords, providers, and a validated video key (or `video: null`)
App loads seed.json with Wi-Fi off
Schema reviewed by C

agent.goal: A committed seed.json of ~60 movies with validated YouTube keys. This is the offline safety net the whole demo rests on, and it gates #12 and #15.
files: scripts/curate.mjs — the curation script (Node, runs once, output committed)
examples/seed.sample.json — the shape to match, already in the repo
steps: Pick ~60 recognisable, visually varied titles. Judges must recognise them on sight.
For each: GET /movie/{id}?append_to_response=videos,watch/providers,keywords with the TMDB bearer.
Video key preference order is Clip > Teaser > Trailer, site == 'YouTube', official == true where available. Fall back to a YouTube Data API v3 search restricted to the Movieclips channel.
VALIDATE every key with YouTube videos.list part=status,contentDetails: embeddable === true, not region-blocked for US, not age-restricted. An unvalidated key is a black rectangle in front of judges.
Set start to skip studio logos (5–10s is usually right) and end at start+15..20s.
Write { key, start, end, source } or video: null. A null video is fine — the card falls back to the poster (#7).
Map providers from watch/providers.results.US.flatrate[].provider_name.
Commit lib/seed.json. C reviews the schema against types/movie.ts (#5) before it is considered done.
agent.contract: Output must satisfy the Movie[] interface in examples/types.ts exactly — id, title, year, genreIds, genreNames, keywords, poster, providers, video. #12 reads genreIds and keywords; #15 returns this shape.
gotchas: Never download, rehost or clip the video files themselves. Keys only — this is the legal decision the whole project rests on (AGENTS.md §3).
The end field is advisory: the IFrame API cannot reliably hard-stop at a timestamp, so #7 loops via seekTo(start) on ended.
poster must be the full https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w780/... URL, not the bare path, so the app never string-concatenates it.
verify: node scripts/curate.mjs writes ~60 entries
Every non-null video key loads in a browser embed
The app reads seed.json with Wi-Fi off

issues.title: Taste vector + scoring model
issues.desc: Weighted feature dict over TMDB genre ids + keywords + top cast. Like → +w on the movie's features, dislike → −w. score(m) = Σ tasteVector[f] for f in features(m), normalized by feature count. Re-rank remaining deck after each swipe.
ac: Liking two action movies moves action titles up the deck
Disliking demotes
Runs in < 5 ms for 60 movies

agent.goal: The recommendation engine. Small, synchronous, no network — and the single biggest unlock in the project: seven issues wait on it.
steps: features(movie) → string[]: genreIds map to 'genre:28', keywords to 'keyword:heist', top-3 cast to 'cast:3223'. Exactly the key format frozen in #5.
applySwipe(vector, movie, dir): like adds +w to each feature, dislike subtracts. w = 1 is fine; weight genres slightly above keywords if you want a knob.
score(vector, movie): sum vector[f] over features(movie), normalized by features.length so long-keyword movies do not dominate.
rank(vector, movies): sort by score descending, return a new array — never mutate the deck in place.
Keep it pure and synchronous. Persistence is #18's job, Firestore never appears in this file.
gotchas: Must run under 5ms for 60 movies — it re-ranks on every swipe, inside the gesture. No async, no I/O.
Freeze this signature early and tell B and A. Changing it after #17 and #18 are underway costs more than it saves.
verify: Liking two action films moves action titles up the deck
Disliking demotes
console.time shows <5ms for 60 movies

issues.title: TMDB fetch layer with seed fallback
issues.desc: `/discover/movie` + `/movie/{id}?append_to_response=videos,watch/providers` mapped to the Movie type. Prefer Clip > Teaser > Trailer for the video key. On any error or offline, return seed.json.
ac: Returns ≥ 20 movies with video keys when online
Wi-Fi off → seed data, no error surfaced to the user

agent.goal: One catalog API for the whole app that never fails loudly — online it is TMDB, offline it is seed.json, and callers cannot tell the difference.
steps: getDeck(filters?) → /discover/movie with the v4 bearer; then hydrate each result with /movie/{id}?append_to_response=videos,watch/providers,keywords.
Map into the Movie type from #5. Video key preference: Clip > Teaser > Trailer, site 'YouTube'.
Wrap every call: on ANY error, timeout, or offline, return seed.json mapped through the same mapper. The user must never see an error state — that is the AC.
Add a short timeout (3s). A hanging TMDB call on venue wifi is the same as an outage and must fall back just as fast.
Cache hydrated movies in memory by id so re-ranking never refetches.
gotchas: TMDB rate limit is generous (~40-50 req/s) but hydrating 60 movies is 60 calls — batch and cache, do not refetch per swipe.
Attribution is contractual and lands in #27 — do not skip it.
Venue wifi is the documented top risk. The offline path is not theoretical; #26 tests it for real.

issues.title: Group session + join code (Firestore realtime)
issues.desc: Create `sessions/{code}` (4-letter code). Members write to `sessions/{code}/members/{uid}` with their likes/dislikes. Every device subscribes with onSnapshot.
ac: Two devices join the same code and see the member list update live
Swipes appear in Firestore within ~1s

agent.goal: Two phones in one session, seeing each other live. Everything about the group demo depends on this working over venue wifi.
steps: createSession() → 4-letter code, uppercase, no vowels (avoids accidental words) — write sessions/{code} with createdAt and hostUid.
joinSession(code) → write sessions/{code}/members/{uid} with empty likes/dislikes.
recordSwipe(code, movieId, dir) → update the member doc's likes/dislikes arrays (arrayUnion).
subscribe(code, cb) → onSnapshot over sessions/{code}/members, delivering Member[] on every change. #17 consumes this.
Handle rejoin: the same uid joining twice must not duplicate a member or wipe their swipes.
Show the code large on screen — judges and your second phone both need to read it.
gotchas: Swipes must reach Firestore within ~1s — batch nothing, write on each swipe.
Anonymous uid must exist before any write (#2). A null uid throws a permissions error that looks like a Firestore bug.
Unsubscribe on unmount or you will leak listeners across rehearsal runs.
verify: Two devices on one code see the member list update live

issues.title: Match detection (Average-without-Misery) + persist match
issues.desc: Compute each member's per-title score; rank by Average-without-Misery (exclude any title a member swiped left / scored below threshold); tie-break by mutual-like count. Emit a match event when a title crosses the mutual threshold. On match, write `{tmdbId, sessionCode, matchedAt}` to every member's `users/{uid}/matches` so it shows in the Saved tab.
ac: A mutual like triggers the match event on all devices
A vetoed title never wins
Match document exists for every member after the reveal

agent.goal: The algorithm that decides the group's film and fires the match event on every phone. Step 4 of the demo path.
steps: For each candidate title, compute every member's score via score() from #12 — reuse it, do not reimplement scoring here.
Average-without-Misery: DROP any title that any member swiped left on or scored below a floor. Then rank the survivors by mean score. A vetoed title must never win — that is an explicit AC.
Tie-break by mutual-like count.
Emit the match when a title crosses the mutual threshold (every member liked it, or the top survivor once all members have swiped N cards).
Write the match to sessions/{code}/match AND to each member's users/{uid}/matches so #41's Saved tab shows it for everyone.
The match doc is the single source of truth — every device reacts to the doc, never to its own local swipe.
gotchas: Fire the Gemini compromise call (#21) at DETECTION time, not at reveal time, so the why text is ready when the reveal mounts.
Guard against double-firing: once sessions/{code}/match exists, do not overwrite it.
Depends on #12's score() — if that signature moves, this breaks silently.
verify: A mutual like triggers the reveal on both devices
A title one member vetoed never wins
A match doc exists under every member's uid
